notes.title: Update 0.8.0.5
notes.notes:
Hello Anomaly Observers,
First of all we want to thank you for your feedback! Your feedback helped make this update

which will improve your anomaly-hunting experience:

Added intruder camera angle (for now only in House contract)

Added new intruder

Major overhaul of House contract

Lowered price of most shop items

Significantly increased chance of special anomalies and intruders happening during contracts

Incrased money gained per contract by ~25%

Game stage 2 will now happen earlier

Decreased glitching effect of intruders appearing



Thanks for playing and keep those anomalies in check!

notes.title: Minor Update 0.8.0.1 – Quality of Life Improvements
notes.notes:
Hello Anomaly Observers,
We’re rolling out a small update to improve your anomaly-hunting experience:

Reports now apply to the original room where they were submitted, preventing failures caused by camera shifts.

You can now freely move the camera while submitting a report.

Adjusted the size of the Office Chair in the Living Room in House Contract for better visual consistency.

Thanks for playing and keep those anomalies in check!

notes.title: An Important Update on Anomaly Observer
notes.notes:
Hello Anomaly Observers,

We’ve got a major update to share regarding the release of Anomaly Observer. After much reflection and discussion within our team, we’ve decided to shift our release strategy: instead of launching the full version, we will be releasing the game in Early Access.


Why the Change?
Our vision for Anomaly Observer has evolved. While the game is already fully playable and offers a compelling experience, we believe that involving the community earlier will help us take it even further. Early Access allows us to:

Gather feedback from real players

Improve gameplay balance and polish

Add new content based on your suggestions

Build a stronger, more connected community


What to Expect in Early Access
The Early Access version will include:

The full core gameplay experience

All contracts

All major features already implemented

However, there may still be bugs, and some areas will benefit from refinement. We’ll be actively updating the game based on your feedback.


What Comes Next?
We plan to stay in Early Access for approximately 6 months, during which we’ll:

Add new content and features

Polish visuals and performance

Improve localization and accessibility

Respond to community feedback

Once we feel the game has reached its full potential, we’ll launch version 1.0 with a price increase to reflect the added value.


Join Us on This Journey
We’re incredibly excited to open the doors to Anomaly Observer and invite you to be part of its evolution. Your feedback will shape the future of the game, and we can’t wait to hear what you think.

Thank you for your support—and welcome to the anomaly.

notes.title: Anomaly Observer Demo Public Release
notes.notes:
Greetings fellow Anomaly Observers,

We're thrilled to announce the public release of the Anomaly Observer Demo, now available to all curious minds and fearless souls. Developed with a deep love for atmospheric tension and psychological horror, Anomaly Observer invites players into a surreal world where nothing is quite what it seems—and you're not just watching. You're being watched.



In this first playable demo, you'll:

Take on the role of the Anomaly Observer, an employee watching CCTV cameras in an unsettling environment that reveals more than meets the eye.

Piece together a fractured reality through eerie encounters, subtle clues, and chilling anomalies.

Experience immersive gameplay mechanics inspired by classic observation horror titles with many different mechanics.



What the demo contains:

One Contract set in House where you will investigate continuously mysterious happenings

Four purchasable items

Three different game modes to experience the House Contract in many different ways

7 Achievements

Leaderboards - become the best Anomaly Observer!



The demo offers a taste of what’s to come: cryptic ambiance, and a sense of creeping dread that stays with you long after you’ve stopped playing.
